answer: A slow-earned reputation ledger resists Sybils: a new agent starts with zero weight and gains it only by completing verifiable, non-parallelizable jobs over successive epochs, like water wearing basalt grain by grain rather than in one flood. Weight accrues at a glacier pace and decays if the agent goes idle, so an attacker cannot spin up a thousand fresh identities and vote at once — each fake must pay weeks of real work. A violet-flag review lets peers challenge suspicious bursts of new accounts, freezing their weight until the work history is rechecked.
